text:
Cole Caufield has 12 goals in 23 games, a little behind the pace of last season's 51, and against Boston it gets silly: Ty Anderson noted he was the first player since Auston Matthews with 12 goals in a 12-game stretch against the Bruins. His own shooting is a reasonable 15.8%, and he's 11th among 547 skaters in wins added.

The caution is around him rather than in him. Montreal has scored 6.1 more goals than its chances deserve with Caufield on the ice, and at five on five his line is getting outchanced (48.6% of expected goals). His last ten (8 points against 9.2 expected) already show a little of that cooling.

The case for the goals lasting is where he shoots from. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile for scoring chances from the slot last season, and he gets a lot of shots off passes across the royal road. Last season Evolving-Hockey had his expected wins well above his actual ones; this year the finishing is catching up.
headline: Caufield's goals are fine; the bounces around him aren't
